title: Rav Chana bar Chimi
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: R' Pedat said in R' Yochanan's name: ‘Whoever satisfies himself with words of Torah, or recites the Shema on his bed and goes to sleep, will not receive bad tidings.’ Hyman's own reading in Berakhot 14a is Rav Acha, son of R' Chiya bar Abba, reporting R' Yochanan.

notes.text: The heading is not explicitly joined to the opening Pedat attribution. The consulted Berakhot paragraph has Rav Acha reporting Rabbi Chiya, who reports Rabbi Yochanan, whereas Hyman abbreviates this to Acha reporting Yochanan. The source-chain question remains open without inserting an unprinted link into the body.

The saved whole Vilna1861 Sheiltot29:1 scalar actually has abbreviated Chana bar Chimi reporting Pedat reporting Yochanan and the Torah-or-bedtime-Shema saying, linking the heading to this transmission without inserting missing source words in the body. All those exact title markers are abbreviated, not new full Rabbi evidence. Supplied heading Rav and body Rav Acha remain full; uninspected Chiya’s title stays R'. The earlier Berakhot14a reporting-chain difference remains disclosed, and Hyman’s our reading refers to his text. The saying remains a quoted tradition, not an independently verified promise.

The printed notice (vol. II, p. 464) has a separate heading for Chana bar Chimi. Sheiltot 29:1 names him reporting Pedat, who reports Yochanan, with Torah or bedtime Shema followed by staying the night. Its following dream saying names Chana bar Hinda separately. In the consulted Berakhot 14a paragraph, Acha son of Chiya bar Abba reports Chiya, who reports Yochanan. That paragraph gives the Torah-and-sleep wording. Hyman’s shorter wording of the comparison is retained.
